rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING ANIMAL HEALTH, PROVIDING MEASURES FOR THE DETECTION, PREVENTION, CONTROL AND ERADICATION OF CERTAIN DISEASES AFFECTING LIVESTOCK AND OTHER ANIMALS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Animal Health Code of 2003\". The spread of notifiable diseases (food and mouth disease (FMD), hog cholera, newcastle disease) among livestock and other animals threatens food security and the viability of the livestock industry. The bill aims to promote animal health by providing measures for the detection, prevention, control and eradication of diseases affecting livestock and other animals. It provides for the codification of all existing laws, rules and regulations pertaining to the prevention, control and eradication of infectious animal diseases.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2003-10-24

rows.author: D051
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE MANUFACTURE, REPAIR, REQUALIFICATION, SALE AND DISTRIBUTION OF LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) CYLINDERS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The LPG Cylinder Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"LPG Cylinder Act of 2003\". To protect the interests of the consumers, the bill seeks to ensure that appropriate standards will be developed and formulated for the Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) industry. It mandates the Department of Trade and Industry, as the lead agency in the implementation of the proposed law, to establish an LPG cylinder development program and undertake research, standardization, promotion, market monitoring, certification, testing, accreditation and enforcement activities. The measure also provides for penalties and fines for violations of the law.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06

rows.author: B024
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EXTEND THE UTILIZATION PERIOD OF THE AGRICULTURAL COMPETITIVENESS ENHANCEMENT FUND, AMENDING SECTION 8 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8178, ENTITLED \"AN ACT REPLACING QUANTITATIVE IMPORT RESTRICTION ON AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS, EXCEPT RICE, WITH TARIFFS, CREATING THE AGRICULTURAL COMPETITIVENESS ENHANCEMENT FUND, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Agricultural Competitiveness Enhancement Fund (ACEF) which was created under R.A. 8178, was granted a life span of nine years. However, the ACEF was not disbursed according to the intended purpose but instead the money collected for the ACEF from 1996 to 1998 was utilized for budgetary support. The measure urges the extension of the utilization period of the ACEF by ten years to enable the government to provide the agricultural and fishery sectors the opportunity to use the funds to strengthen their development activities. The availability of the ACEF will relieve farmers of the need to secure other funds for their competitive enhancement activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2003-11-12

rows.author: C082
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE MEDIATION CENTER FOR COURT-ANNEXED MEDIATION CASES, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Mediation Center Act\". Since its creation in 2001 through a Supreme Court resolution, the Philippine Mediation Center (PMC) has been successful in promoting court-annexed mediation as an effective alternative dispute resolution mechanism in de-clogging court dockets. Areas with PMC units have registered high settlement rates. However, the effectiveness of court-annexed mediation is limited by the small number of PMC units across the country. This bill seeks to institutionalize and constitute a permanent PMC in order to make court-annexed mediation available to the general public.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-11-12

rows.author: C097
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING THE DIRECTORS OF LOCAL WATER DISTRICTS TO RECEIVE OTHER ALLOWANCES AND/OR BENEFITS AND PROVIDING SECURITY OF TENURE TO GENERAL MANAGERS OF LOCAL WATER DISTRICTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 13 AND 23 OF THE \"PROVINCIAL WATER UTILITIES ACT OF 1973\", AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: P.D. 198 (Provincial Water utilities Act of 1973) expressly prohibits directors of local water districts (LWDs) from receiving other compensation for services rendered to the district. Directors of LWDs are granted a per diem of fifty pesos only for each board meeting actual attended but not more than four meetings for each month. P.D. 198 also provided that the LWD's general manager who is appointed by the Board of Directors, shall serve at the pleasure of the board. While the general manager has full supervision and control of the operation of local water facilities, with the power and authority to appoint the personnel of the district, he does not enjoy security of tenure. The bill seeks to provide security of tenure to general managers and allow directors to receive other allowances and/or benefits commensurate to their responsibilities and at par with the present cost of living.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2003-11-12

rows.author: D102
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE RETIREMENT BENEFITS OF PRIVATE SECTOR EMPLOYEES, AMENDING ARTICLE 287 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Our senior citizens deserve a comfortable and secure retirement life free from the worries of providing for one's basic needs. This bill aims to increase the workers' retirement pay to enable our senior citizens to retire in reasonable comfort and convenience after putting in years of work for the profit of others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-11-12

rows.author: D102
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING LABOR-ONLY CONTRACTING AND RATIONALIZING THE SCOPE OF JOB-CONTRACTING, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 106, 280 AND 281 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Tenure in employment means the right to continue in employment until the same is terminated for a just or authorized cause. However, it has become very difficult for the work force to gain a regular employee status thus the right to security of tenure remains unrealizable for many. The measure proposes to concretize the right of workers to security of tenure. It also penalizes labor-only contracting and limits the scope of permissible job-contracting.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-11-12

rows.author: D102
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING ALL EMPLOYEES OF ALL BRANCHES, SUBDIVISIONS, INSTRUMENTALITIES AND AGENCIES OF THE GOVERNMENT, INCLUDING GOVERNMENT-OWNED OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS WITH OR WITHOUT ORIGINAL CHARTERS THE RIGHT TO ENGAGE IN PEACEFUL AND CONCERTED ACTIVITIES INCLUDING THE RIGHT TO STRIKE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 244 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The right of government employees to self-organization differs significantly with that of private sector employees. While Executive Order No. 180, series of 1986, grants government employees the right to form and join organizations of their own choosing, it does not, however, grant government employees the right to collective bargaining and to engage in concerted activities including the right to strike. To correct this discrimination against government employees, the bill grants all employees of all branches, subdivisions, instrumentalities and agencies of the government, including government-owned or controlled corporations with or without original charters the right to engage in peaceful concerted activities, including the right to strike, for purposes of collective bargaining for their mutual benefit and protection.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-11-12

rows.author: D102
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 264(e) OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The right of workers to strike and engage in other concerted activities is blunted by the proscription against obstructing free ingress to or egress from the employer's premises for lawful purposes. A strike or any concerted action is rendered inutile when the employer is able to surreptitiously transfer raw materials or equipment or even scabs during labor disputes. The bill proposes to strengthen the rights of workers to strike and at the same time protect the rights of persons who are strangers to the labor dispute. It declares as unlawful for an employee to remove from or bring into the business premises machines or other equipment, raw materials, documents and other papers connected with the employer's business, and other items analogous to the foregoing.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-11-12

rows.author: D102
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 257 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill aims to strengthen the right of workers to self-organization through the automatic certification of uncontested unions as exclusive bargaining agent. It seeks to amend Article 257 of the Labor Code of the Philippines to provide that \"WHERE THERE IS NO OTHER LEGITIMATE LABOR ORGANIZATION FILING A SIMILAR PETITION OR ONE FOR INTERVENTION THEREIN, THE PETITIONING UNION SHALL AUTOMATICALLY BE CERTIFIED BY THE MED-ARBITER AS THE EXCLUSIVE BARGAINING AGENT OF ALL WORKERS IN THE BARGAINING UNIT...\" Through automatic certification of lone union-candidates in unorganized establishments, it is foreseen that collective bargaining will be bolstered without prejudicing the will of the employees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-11-12

rows.author: D102
rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING FURTHER THE POWER OF ASSUMPTION OR CERTIFICATION OF LABOR DISPUTES BY THE SECRETARY OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT BY LIMITING THE EXERCISE THEREOF TO INDUSTRIES FULFILLING ESSENTIAL SERVICES, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 263(g) OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The right of workers to strike has been emasculated by the power granted to the Secretary of Labor, under Article 263 (g) of the Labor Code of the Philippine, to assume jurisdiction over labor disputes causing or likely to cause, in his opinion, a strikeor lockout in an industry deemed to be indispensable to the national interest. The bill aims to rationalize this virtually unfettered discretion granted to the Secretary of Labor to assume jurisdiction over labor disputes by limiting such power to those work establishments that may truly be considered as fulfilling essential services such as hospitals, water supply and electrical services, the lack of which would endanger life or public safety.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-11-12

rows.author: D031
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ABOLISH THE PENALTY OF IMPRISONMENT IN LIBEL AND DEFAMATION CASES AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 355, 356, 357 AND 360 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The measure seeks to abolish the penalty of imprisonment in crimes against honor and to impose instead fines ranging from Ph20,000 to Ph2.0 million. It also proposes to spread the responsibility for the creation and publication or broadcast of news to include the publishers/owners and top management of newspapers, magazines and radio and television stations. By making the publisher/owners and managers equally responsible for the printed article or broadcast, editors and other supervising personnel are compelled to double check stories for elements of libel and oral defamation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-11-12

rows.author: D031
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECRIMINALIZING LIBEL, AND FOR SUCH PURPOSE REPEALING ARTICLES 353, 354, 355, 356, 357, 360, 361 AND 362 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: Experience shows that the threat of imprisonment has not served as an effective deterrent to reckless and irresponsible journalism. The measure proposes to decriminalize libel. Responsible journalism can be better encouraged with a penalty of civil damages in lieu of penal sanctions.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING DIRECT AND TECHNICAL SMUGGLING AS ACTS OF ECONOMIC SABOTAGE, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Declaring Direct and Technical Smuggling as Acts of Economic Sabotage
rows.abstract: To minimize the incidence of smuggling and technical smauggling, the measure seeks to declare the acts of outright/direct smuggling and technical smuggling of a minimum aggregate amount or value of Ph 1.0 million as acts of economic sabotage. It provides for penalties such as: a) fine equal to the value of the smuggled articles; b) fine equal to the aggregate amount of the taxes, duties and other charges avoided; c) imprisonment of a minimum eight years and one day; and d) confiscation of the smuggled articles. The measure further grants the Bureau of Customs additional powers for the disposition of the confiscated goods.

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT GOVERNING THE ESTABLISHMENT, OPERATION AND REGULATION OF LENDING COMPANIES
rows.title_short: The Lending Company Regulation Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Lending Company Regulation Act of 2003\". Lending companies (LCs) or lending investors are primarily engaged in extending credit to its clients through direct loans or direct lending. Direct lending has been defined in the Financing Act of 1998 as among the activities of a financing company hence LCs fall under the regulation and supervision of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). However, not all LCs are organized as corporations hence the SEC can not regulate those organized as single proprietorship since these are registered with the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI). The bill seeks to require all LCs to register as corporations and allow existing LCs organized as single proprietorship or partnerships to convert into corporations within one year from the effectivity of this act. It also delineates the authority of the SEC and the DTI over LCs.
rows.status: Business for the day on 2003-11-19

rows.author: C113
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO LIBERALIZE THE OPERATIONS OF RURAL BANKS AMENDING FOR THAT PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7353, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'RURAL BANKS ACT OF 1992'
rows.title_short: Liberalizing the Operations of Rural Banks, Amending for the Purpose RA 7353
rows.abstract: To provide adequate credit facilities to farmers and merchants, or to cooperatives of such farmers and merchants; and to promote rural savings, the bill seeks to liberalize the operations of rural banks by introducing the following amendments, among others, to the Rural Banks Act of 1992: a) consider rural banks which have extended 8% of loan portfolio to small enterprises as being in full compliance of the small and medium credit mandatory allocation provided in RA 6977, as amended by RA 8289; b) liberalization of the nationality requirement to allow former Philippine nationals to acquire capital stock in rural banks; c) exemption of rural banks from the independent capital requirement; d) exemption of rural banks from the payment of gross receipts tax or value-added tax for a period of ten years.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING NOVEMBER TWENTY-FIVE OF EVERY YEAR AS NATIONAL CONSCIOUSNESS DAY FOR THE ELIMINATION OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN
rows.abstract: On November 25, 1960, the Mirabal sisters, who were involved in activities against the Trujillo dictatorship in the Dominican Republic, were assassinated in an \"accident\". Since their death, the sisters have become the symbol of the victimization of women. As far back as 1999, women organizations in the country have commemorated November 25 as the International Day Against Violence Against Women with consciousness raising activities highlighting the issues of violence against women. These activities were centered mainly in key cities. To foster a nationwide observance, this bill proposes to declare November 25 of every year as a National Consciousness Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-11-28

rows.author: D028
rows.title_full: AN ACT LIMITING THE NUMBER OF FILIPINO-FOREIGNER PLAYING IN ANY PROFESSIONAL BASKETBALL LEAGUE IN THE PHILIPPINES TO TWO FOR EACH TEAM
rows.abstract: Most of our youth dream of becoming basketball players in the Philippine Basketball Association (PBA). However, the presence of Filipino-foreigners playing in the PBA has greatly diminished the chances of home-grown talents to become players in the PBA. Furthermore, the presence of Filipino-foreigner players has led to demoralization among full-blooded Filipino players who receive considerably lower professional fees than the Filipino-foreigner players. This bill seeks to limit the number of Filipino-foreigner players in the professional basket leagues in the Philippines to two per basketball team to minimize the undesirable effects of the proliferation of Filipino-foreigner players.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GAMES AND AMUSEMENTS since 2003-11-18

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS ON THE INCOME REQUIREMENT FOR THE CREATION OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.title_short: Amending Certain Sections on the Income Requirement for the Creation of Local Government Units
rows.abstract: R.A. 9009 increased the income requirement for the creation of municipalities into cities from PhP 20 million to Ph100 million while the income requirement for the creation of provinces and highly urbanized cities remained at PhP 20 million and Ph 50 million, respectively. The bill seeks to correct this imbalance in the income requirement by excluding the internal revenue allotment (IRA) shares in the computation of local income. It further maintained the income requirement for the conversion of municipalities into cities at P 20 million as stipulated in the Local Government Code provided only locally generated incomes are included in the computation of the income requirement.

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1949, ENTITLED \"ESTABLISHING A JUDICIARY DEVELOPMENT FUND\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In order to democratize the use of the Judiciary Development Fund (JDF), the measure proposes to increase the apportionment for the cost of living allowance of the members and personnel of the Judiciary from 80% to 90% of the JDF and to proportionately lower from 20% to 10% the allocation for the acquisition, maintenance and repair of office equipment and facilities in court where the legal fees were collected. The bill also seeks to transfer the administration and allocation of the JDF from the Chief Justice to the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court shall have the exclusive power and duty to approve the authorized disbursements and expenditures  of the JDF in accordance with set guidelines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2003-11-19

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROFESSIONALIZATION OF THE BUREAU OF FIRE PROTECTION (BFP) AND THE BUREAU OF JAIL MANAGEMENT AND PENOLOGY (BJMP)
rows.title_short: Bureau of Fire Protection and Bureau of Jail Management and Penology PRofessionalization Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Bureau of Fire Protection and Bureu of Jail Management and Penology Professionalization Act of 2003\". The bill aims to professionalize and restructure the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) and the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) by upgrading the qualification standards of their uniformed personnel and place them at par with their counterpart in the Philippine National Police and the Armed Forces of the Philippines. It directs the Department of the Interior and Local Government to design a professionalization and qualifications upgrading program for the uniformed personnel of the BFP and the BJMP.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09263) enacted on 2004-03-10

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE UPGRADING OF THE RATES OF COMPENSATION OF THE OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE JUDICIARY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Judiciary Compensation Restructure Act of 2003\". R.A. 9227 granted special monthly allowances equivalent to 100% of their basic salaries to justices and judges. However, court officers and employees, who perform the bulk of the tasks needed to dispense justice, were not given any additional allowance or increase in their salaries. This has caused widespread demoralization in the ranks of court personnel. This bill seeks to provide for the upgrading of the rates of compensation of the officers and employees of the Judiciary by one salary grade.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2003-11-19

rows.author: D096
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION OF TAXI COMPANY ACTIVITIES AND PROVIDING THE MECHANICS FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION
rows.abstract: \"Taxi Transport Practices Regulation Act of 2003\". Taxi companies are mandated by their franchise agreement with the Land Transportation Franchising Regulatory Board to convey their passengers to any destination according to the latter's instructions. However, abusive taxi drivers and operators constantly violate this agreement by not conveying passengers citing heavy traffic or too distant destinations as excuses. The measure aims to subject taxi operators and drivers harsher penalties should they commit acts in violation of their franchise agreement. It also provides a mechanism whereby the government can immediately deal with such violations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2003-11-19

rows.author: D046
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL GOVERNMENT ISSUED IDENTIFICATION CARDS, CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES TO INCLUDE A PORTION INDICATING THE BLOOD TYPE OF THE HOLDER THEREOF AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: \"Blood Type Identification Act of 2003\". Statistics show that many accident victims die or suffer physical disabilities or complications because much-needed blood can not be transferred to them at once. This bill aims to require all government issued identification cards, certificates and licenses (e.g. SSS card, GSIS card, birth certificate, driver's license, firearms license, professional license, etc.) to indicate the blood type of the owner-holder thereof. With the information, blood transfusion delays caused by blood type ignorance can be prevented.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2003-11-19

rows.author: D046
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PUBLIC EXHIBITION OR DISPLAY OF OBSCENE AND/OR DISTRACTIVE MOTION OR STILL PICTURES ALONG MAJOR THOROUGHFARES
rows.abstract: Obscene and/or distractive pictures-billboards advertising products, movies and services have sprouted like mushrooms in our major thoroughfares such as the Epifanio delos Santos Avenue, Aurora Boulevard, South Expressway and the North Luzon Expressway. The presence of these obscene billboards have proven to be hazardous to road safety and to have damaging effects on the values of children and the general public. This bill seeks to prohibit the public display of obscene pictures, whether motion or still, along major thoroughfares and provides penalties for those responsible for the public exhibition or display.

rows.author: B020
rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE PREMIUM TAX AND AMENDING THE DOCUMENTARY STAMP TAX ON LIFE INSURANCE POLICIES, ANNUITIES AND PRE-NEED PLANS, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 123 AND AMENDING SECTIONS 183 AND 186 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
rows.title_short: Abolishing the Premium Tax and Amending the Documentary Stamp Tax on Life Insurance Policies, Annuities and Pre-Need Plans
rows.abstract: The life insurance industry is a vital source of long-term savings, However, the heavy taxes currently imposed on the industry serve as a disincentive to buy life insurance and   the generation of much needed savings for the economy. This bill pushes for the abolition of the premium tax on life insurance policies. Likewise, it seeks to amend Section 183 of the National Internal Revenue Code by adding a provision that no documentary stamp tax (DST) shall be imposed if the premium paying period for insurance policies and annuities exceeds five years. Furthermore, it shall also provide that no DST shall be imposed on all pre-need plans if the premium paying period is at least five years. The abolition of the premium tax and the non-imposition of the DST would boost the growth of the domestic insurance market.
rows.status: Business for the day on 2003-11-19

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ACT NO. 4103, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE INDETERMINATE SENTENCE LAW
rows.abstract: Penal laws are viewed as reformatory, retributory and a deterrent. However, these objectives becomes irrelevant in the case of septuagenarians since their reformation and rehabilitation would be of no value to themselves, their family and even to society unless they are given a chance to live with their families. This measure aims to make prisoners who are seventy five (75) years of age or above eligible to parole provided that there is a reasonable probability that such prisoner will remain at liberty without violating the law and that such release will not be incompatible with the welfare of the society.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-11-19

rows.author: D047
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING VOLUNTEERISM AND ITS INSTITUTIONALIZATION AS A STRATEGY FOR NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Volunteer Act of 2003\". Over the years, the government has recognized the merging role of the voluntary sector as an effective partner in national and international development undertakings. This bill seeks to strengthen volunteerism in the country by establishing a conducive policy environment that will provide the venue for its promotion, advocacy and institutionalization in the various sectors in order to harmonize the diverse volunteer efforts into an effective partner for national and international development.

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: AN ACT RECOGNIZING THE RIGHTS OF LESBIANS AND GAYS, PROVIDING MECHANISMS FOR THE PROTECTION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Magna Carta for Lesbians and Gays\". Despite many international and national legal prohibitions, discrimination against cultural minorities, children, women, migrants, the disabled and people who have other sexual orientation is still pervasive in our society. Discrimination is much more glaring in the case of gays and lesbians who are often portrayed in the tri-media as second class citizens. They are forced to live with harassment, neglect, exploitation and indifference. This bill aims to promote the interests, rights and welfare of Filipino lesbians and gays by guaranteeing their rights to equal opportunity and treatment in employment; access to public services and accommodations; education; primary health care; and access to military, police and other similar institutions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL, POLITICAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS since 2003-11-19

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AN ELECTIVE OFFICIAL IPSO FACTO RESIGNED FROM HIS OFFICE UPON THE FILING OF HIS CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY
rows.abstract: Ra 9006 (Fair Election Practices Act) allows any elective public official to run for any public office other than the one he is holding without the risk of losing said office. This is contrary to the constitutional edict for all public official to serve the people with utmost loyalty and not trifle with the mandate which their constituent  have entrusted to them. This bill seeks to declare any elective official whether national or local, running for any public office other than the one he is holding as ipso facto resigned from his office upon the filing of the certificate of candidacy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2003-11-25

rows.author: D074
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE MT. GUITING-GUITING NATURAL PARK LOCATED IN SIBUYAN ISLAND, PROVINCE OF ROMBLON, AS A PROTECTED AREA AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Establishing the Mt. Guiting-guiting Natural Park in Sibuyan Island, Romblon as a PRotected Area

rows.author: C130
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2004-02-05, transmitted to on 2004-02-09 and received by the Senate on 2004-02-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 261 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In the past elections, it has been the practice of the New People's Army (NPA), its members and allied organizations to demand or extort money or other valuable considerations from candidates running for public office in exchange for \"permits to campaign\" and the like. The \"permit to campaign\" would allow candidate to campaign freely inside the NPA's claimed \"territories\". This practice goes against the principles of human rights, political freedom and of electoral reform. This measure seeks to render much practice on electoral offense under our electoral laws (Batas Pambansa Blg. 881)
rows.status: Substituted by HB06676

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL OWNERS OR OPERATORS OF TELEVISION NETWORKS OR STATIONS AND PRODUCERS OF TELEVISION NEWS PROGRAMS TO BROADCAST THEIR NEWS PROGRAMS WITH SUBTITLES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.title_short: Requiring Owners or Operators of Television Networks or Stations and Producers of Television News Programs to Broadcast Their News Programs With Substitles
rows.abstract: Television and motion pictures are the most popular means of communication in the world. They influence the lives of many people. Unfortunately, individual with hearing impairment are denied the opportunity to fully enjoy and appreciate watching television or viewing a film. This bill seeks to require all franchise holders, operators and producers of domestic television stations and television programs, home video programs and motion pictures to air their programs and films with closed captions for the benefit of the hearing impaired.
rows.status: Business for the day on 2003-12-08

rows.author: C106
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE CONSULTING SERVICES BOARD IN ORDER TO UPGRADE AND PROFESSIONALIZE THE CONSULTING SERVICES IN THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Consulting services are essential to the country's development. However, the access of Filipino consultant to foreign funded projects in the country is often at the mercy of their foreign counterparts. Also, with the country's accession to the World Trade Organization, better opportunities have opened abroad for the services of Filipino professional consultants. This bill aims to provide the platform for deserving Filipino consultants to have equal footing with their foreign counterparts in the practice of their profession not only in the Philippines but elsewhere in the world. It seeks to establish the Consulting Services Board which shall be tasked to professionalize and upgrade the standing of Filipino consultants to reasonable, if not equal footing  with their foreign counterparts.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-12-01

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING MALL AND STORE OWNERS ENGAGING IN THE SALE OF CONTRABAND PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: Piracy and smuggling of product is not only hurting the country's image internationally but it also affects our local performers and manufacturers. Smuggling and pirated goods distort normal pricing mechanisms and affect market forces. To clamp down on these illegal activities, the bill seeks to impose penalties to store/stall owners who engage in the sale of contraband products and to mall owners who tolerate their tenants to engage in the sale of pirated and smuggled goods.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2003-12-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE INCLUSION OF ALL ELECTRIC COOPERATIVES ORGANIZED AND EXISTING UNDER PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 269, AS AMENDED, AND REGISTERED WITH THE NATIONAL ELECTRIFICATION ADMINISTRATION (NEA) WITHIN THE COVERAGE OF TAX EXEMPTION PRIVILEGES AND INCENTIVES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Sections 193 and 234 of the Local Government Code provide for the withdrawal of tax exemption privileges from electric cooperatives not registered with the Cooperative Development Authority. Such cooperatives are required to pay real property taxes and other fees being imposed by the local government units concerned. The withdrawal of the tax exemptions has resulted in heavy financial burdens which the cooperative, in turn, pass on to consumers. This bill seeks to grant tax exemption privileges and incentives to all electric cooperative organized and existing under P.D. No. 269, as amended, and registered with the National Electrification Administration.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2003-12-08

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8435, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"AN ACT PRESCRIBING URGENT RELATED MEASURES TO MODERNIZE THE AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES SECTORS OF THE COUNTRY IN ORDER TO ENHANCE THEIR PROFITABILITY, AND PREPARE SAID SECTORS FOR THE CHALLENGES OF GLOBALIZATION THROUGH AN ADEQUATE, FOCUSED AND RATIONAL DELIVERY OF NECESSARY SUPPORT SERVICES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The enactment of the Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act (AFMA) effectively deprived the agro-processors of the importation incentives they enjoyed under the Investment Priorities Plan (IPP) such as the duty-free importation of equipment, the availment of equivalent tax credits for locally procured equipment and tax holidays. Believing that agro-processors enjoy these incentives under the AFMA, the Board of investments excluded agro-processors from the IPP. The lost incentive resulted in a decline in investment in agro-processing activities from 2001 until the present. This measure seeks to restore the incentives program, specially the duty-free importation of capital equipment, to the agri-business sector.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2003-12-08

rows.author: B024
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE MEAT INSPECTION SYSTEM IN THE COUNTRY, ORDAINING FOR THIS PURPOSE A 'MEAT INSPECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Meat Inspection Code of the Philippines
rows.abstract: \"The Meat Inspection Code of the Philippines.\" To ensure the safety and fitness for human consumption of all meat and meat products, both in the domestic and international markets, the measure seeks to strengthen and codify the rules and regulations pertaining to the inspection of meat and meat products. It empowers the National Meat Inspection Commission to formulate, issue and implement national policies, guidelines and rules and regulations for the effective implementation of the proposed code.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09296) enacted on 2004-05-12

rows.author: D072
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAMS IN THE PENAL INSTITUTIONS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREOF
rows.abstract: Prisoners upon release from prison should be given the chance to have free and decent lives in the outside world. However, it is a sad reality that ex-prisoners have extreme difficulty in finding jobs. As a result, some of these ex-prisoners have to resort to illegal activities in order to survive, only to end up in jail again. This bill seeks to strengthen the education and training programs in penal institutions. It provides for a complete high school curriculum to enable inmates to complete their secondary education. It also provides for the holding of vocational training for those who have completed high school or college education. With the proper education and training, inmates would be better equipped to engage in small business ventures upon their release.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2003-12-08

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL ALLOWABLE TAX DEDUCTIONS FOR INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 34 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to provide some relief to taxpayer who are married or heads of their families by including rental on their residential  dwellings as an allowable deduction from their gross income for income tax purposes. The said amount may be used by the taxpayer to provide for other equally important needs of his family.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2003-12-09

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE TWENTY PERCENT (20%) FINAL WITHHOLDING TAX IMPOSED UPON THE AMOUNT OF INTEREST FROM ANY CURRENCY BANK DEPOSIT AND YIELD OR ANY OTHER MONETARY BENEFIT FROM DEPOSIT SUBSTITUTES AND FROM TRUST FUNDS AND SIMILAR ARRANGEMENTS AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 24 (B)(1) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Savings generation is the most convenient and inexpensive way of raising capital. However, depositors are dissuaded from putting their money in the bank because of the withholding taxes imposed on interest earnings and the low interest  rates on savings deposits. This bill seeks to abolish the twenty percent (20%) final withholding tax imposed on the interest earnings of any currency bank deposit and yield or any other monetary benefit from deposit substitutes and from trust funds and similar arrangements. The proposed act will help spur economic growth by generating more investment capital sourced from savings deposits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2003-12-09

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING THE PERIOD OF EXEMPTION OF ALL ENTERPRISES ENGAGED IN AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES FROM THE PAYMENT OF TARIFF AND DUTIES FOR THE IMPORTATION OF AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES INPUTS WHICH SHALL INCLUDE ANIMAL FEEDS COMPONENTS AND THEIR SUBSTITUTES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHTY-FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-FIVE OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES MODERNIZATION ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: RA 8435 (Agriculture & Fisheries Modernization Act) instituted various measures and mechanisms for the modernization within the agriculture and fisheries sectors. However, the livestock industry, which is an integral part of the agriculture sector, was excluded from the tariff and duty exemption privilege for importations of animal feeds components such as yellow corn. As a result, the livestock industry and, consequently the entire meat consuming population were prejudiced. This measure seeks to extend the period of exemption of all enterprises engaged in agriculture and fisheries from the payment of tariff and duties for the importation of agriculture and fisheries inputs. It also aims to amend Section 109 of RA 8435 by extending the tariff and duty-free privilege to importation of animal feeds components and their substitutes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2003-12-09

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE CONSULTING SERVICES BOARD IN ORDER TO UPGRADE AND PROFESSIONALIZE THE CONSULTANT SERVICES IN THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Consulting Service Board Law of 2004\". Consulting services, whether established by consulting firms or by individual consultants are essential to the country's sustained development. However, the government has not provided the necessary agency to professionalize consulting services, to put them in equal footing with their foreign counterparts and make them more competitive in the global market. This bill seeks to establish the Consulting Services Board tasked to professionalize the standing of Filipino consultants to put them in equal footing with their foreign counterparts in the practice of their profession not only in the country but also elsewhere.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-12-09
